data.name: Hafizh
data.gender_notes: Hafizh is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who has committed the Quran to memory, known for their knowledge and wisdom. The name Hafizh carries the meaning “Memory keeper, Memorizer” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hafizh usually hope their child will grow to embody memory keeper, memorizer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the pursuit of knowledge and the depth of faith.
data.etymology: Hafizh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Memory keeper, Memorizer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hafizh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_arabic.name: حفيظ
in_arabic.long_meaning: الحافظ هو من أهم أسماء الله الحسنى، وهو ذو معنى غني بالتأمل والتفكر، يشير إلى حفظ القرآن الكريم والدين بأمانة، وهو ما يتمتع به المؤمنون الذين حفظوا الكلام الحق، وتفردوا بالحفظ الذي يفيد الحفاظ على الإيمان في قلوبهم، وتحقيقًا لتلك العلاقة الوثيقة بين الحفظ والإيمان، وهو ما يظهر في آيات قرآنية كثيرة، وهو ما يتمتع به الصالحون والصديقون، وهو ما يفضله العظماء في الأسماء.

in_urdu.meaning: حافظ کتاب و سنت اور دین کا

in_english.name: Hafizh
in_english.meaning: Protector of the Quran and Sunnah, guardian of faith
in_english.long_meaning: Hafizh is one of the most beautiful names of Allah, which is rich in contemplation and thought. It refers to the preservation of the Quran and the Sunnah with a sense of responsibility, which is possessed by believers who have preserved the true word. It is the preserve of those who have preserved their faith in their hearts, and it is the preserve of those who have reserved the preservation of their faith. This preservation is closely related to faith, as shown in many Quranic verses. It is possessed by the righteous and the truthful, and it is the preferred name among the great ones in names.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Hafizh" is deeply rooted in Islamic culture, representing an individual who has dedicated themselves to the sacred preservation and mastery of the Quran through memorization. In traditional Islamic societies, such as parts of the Arab and South Asian regions, being a Hafizh is an achievement worthy of recognition and admiration, as the memorization of the Quran is considered a significant commitment to one's faith and its preservation and propagation. Hafizh communities often come together to share their knowledge and enrich their understanding of the Islamic scripture, fostering a sense of unity and shared commitment to their religious heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: Beyond the cultural significance, the title "Hafizh" carries immense spiritual weight, representing a deep level of connection and devotion to the divine Word of God. Through the act of memorizing the Quran, a Hafizh engages in a sacred partnership with God, forming a bond that is strengthened with each repetition. The mastery and preservation of God's Word also serves as a reminder of the importance of knowledge and learning in one's spiritual journey, reinforcing the belief that seeking and expanding one's knowledge is a lifelong endeavor in the pursuit of growing closer to God.

In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Hafizh serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of memory keeper, memorizer.

historical_references.reference: Hafizh ibn Hibban al-Busti, a prominent scholar in Islamic history, was a renowned hadith scholar and compiler of the Sahih (authentic) Hadith. He lived during the 4th Islamic century, around 350-415 AH (965-1025 AD). He was born in Bostra, Syria and died in Damascus. His most famous work is 'al-Masabih fi Amr il-Sunan wa-Fadlihi' (The Torches Concerning the Sunan and Their Virtues), which contains over 10,000 hadiths. He was given the title 'al-Hafizh' due to his vast knowledge of the hadith collection.

Al-Hafizh Ibn Al-Qayyim, a significant figure in Islamic literature and jurisprudence, was a scholar of Hadith, Sufism, and theology. He lived during the 7th Islamic century, around 691-751 AH (1292-1350 AD). He was born in Damascus, Syria, and died in the same city. He was given the title 'al-Hafizh' due to his extensive knowledge in various Islamic disciplines, particularly in Hadith and Sufism.
historical_references.context: Significant figure in Islamic literature and jurisprudence

modern_usage.modern_context: In the modern context, the title of Hafizh, which is an Islamic honorific for someone who has memorized the entire Quran, is seen as a symbol of dedication, piety, and deep religious commitment. This title is sought after by many Muslims, and various platforms have emerged to facilitate the process of memorization and certification. Mobile apps offer interactive tools and resources to help individuals learn and memorize the Quran at their own pace. Social media platforms provide a community for Hafizh hopefuls to connect with others, share progress, and seek guidance. Online courses offer structured programs and personalized instruction from experienced teachers. Overall, the trend towards memorization of the Quran and the pursuit of the title of Hafizh reflects a deepening commitment to Islamic studies and spiritual growth among many Muslims.
